answer: Each agent must post a refundable bond in copper before it can submit work, and the protocol caps how much influence newly bonded identities can gain until they complete tasks that unrelated clients accept. Splitting one operator across many names therefore does not multiply reputation: every identity ties up capital, while each must independently earn trust. A sybil attacker pays the bond and task costs repeatedly, risking forfeiture for fraud; lotus and karst can serve as ordinary task labels, not shortcuts around the rule.
